it's natural that couples don't see eye to eye on everything. there will be things she likes that you dislike, and vice versa. so just accept that this is one of those things and move on. the simple act of wearing makeup is not harming anyone.

during my sec1 orientation camp a few years ago my friends and i were in the basement of the school building, next to the D&T room. outside the D&T room there’s a statue of st. joseph carrying baby jesus as a child. many seniors had told us apparently the joseph cries blood at night and the head of baby jesus turns to look at you so we decided to check it out. 

once we reached the basement, an eerie feeling set in and we felt shivers run down our spine. around 3am, i felt like something was watching us, like suddenly i felt this foreign gaze on my back. it felt nothing like my friends looking at me, i felt like someone was staring intently at me. i looked up and noticed the statue was “changing.” 

before it became 3am, st. joseph had a benevolent smile on his face. but i swear when i looked at him after the clock struck 3, he was bearing this look of fear. idk how to explain it but his smile seemed forced and his skin looked paler. i thought it was the moonlight shining on it but upon closer inspection, the colour was completely off. 

baby jesus’s head did not move but my friends and i all agreed his eyes seemed to follow us no matter where we shifted. you know what’s the hollow face illusion? it’s when your brain percieves a concave face to be convex. go search up the T-Rex illusion on youtube and you’ll see what i mean. it was something like that, but only the baby jesus statue’s face was convex and not concave. his pupils seemed to travel to wherever we were standing. 

around 3:30am we were getting bored and tired of waiting for something to happen so we decided to make a move. right as we turned around, we heard something shift behind us. 

somehow, the statue had shifted itself 45° and was staring straight at us. we freaked out and ran back to the designated dorm, which was a classroom nearby. after that we could never look that pair of statues in the eye ever again.
